project.name: connected-knowledge
project.description: Short-form videos that build a connected mental model of the world.

content.prompt: Choose one genuinely useful concept from a broad field of knowledge. Prioritize explanatory power over trivia, avoid repeating prior lessons, and connect the idea to other fields when useful. Distinguish established knowledge from uncertainty.
subject_areas: medicine, public health, psychology, and neuroscience
geography, linguistics, religion, archaeology, ecology, agriculture, energy, and urban planning
learning_rules: Gradually increase difficulty and do not repeat lessons.
Use cause-and-effect chains, incentives, tradeoffs, and second-order effects when relevant.
Separate biological, cultural, economic, historical, and institutional explanations.
For history, distinguish consensus from competing interpretations and incomplete evidence.
For science, distinguish consensus, supported theories, emerging evidence, debates, hypotheses, and speculation.

topic_seeds.title: Why incentives can produce unintended outcomes
Why maps change what governments can do

ai_tools.name: research assistant
ai_tools.purpose: Find and summarize authoritative sources; never publish unsupported claims.

ai_tools.name: script model
ai_tools.purpose: Turn approved research into the configured lesson structure.

ai_tools.name: video generator
ai_tools.purpose: Generate or animate visual assets and scenes.

ai_tools.name: editor
ai_tools.purpose: Assemble scenes, narration, music, and captions.
